# Parse typed APIs

Typed Python clients generated by `parse sync` from your Parse APIs. They are installed as the editable `parse_apis` package, so `from parse_apis.<slug> import <Root>` resolves from any directory. Each API's reference is `<slug>/README.md`; APIs marked ✓ below also ship a runnable `<slug>/example.py`.

## APIs

| Import (client) | Summary | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `from parse_apis.phdscanner_com_api import PhDScanner` | Search and browse PhD opportunities and professor postings from PhDScanner.com | ✓ |
| `from parse_apis.scholarshipportal_com_api import ScholarshipPortal` | Search scholarships, academic programmes, universities, and get reference data (countries, disciplines) from StudyPortals/ScholarshipPortal. | ✓ |

## Conventions

- **Import model.** `from parse_apis.<slug> import <Root>`. `parse_apis` is an installed editable package, so this import resolves from any directory — no need to run from a particular folder.
- **Auth.** Construct a client with `api_key=...`, or rely on the configured Parse credentials (`parse login`).
- **Pagination.** List operations return a lazy paginator — iterate it; it fetches pages on demand and stops at the declared boundary. If the upstream refuses deeper pages (a result-window cap), iteration raises `PaginationLimitError` — items already yielded are valid; bound the scan with `limit=`, or catch it (`.list()` attaches the collected items as `err.partial_items`).
- **Field typing is best-effort.** Field types are coerced best-effort at construction; construction never raises. An un-parseable-but-present value is kept RAW — a `float`-typed field may hold a `str` (e.g. `'negotiable'`), and a `bool`-typed field parses common string values like `'false'` / `'0'` without falling back to Python truthiness. A typed field may also be `None` if the scraper did not capture it on this object — e.g. a detail-only field read off a summary is absent there. Validate values you branch on; don't assume the annotation was enforced.
- **Errors.** The runtime error classes (`ParseError`, `AuthError`, `NotFoundError`, `RateLimitError`, `UpstreamError`, `PaginationLimitError`, …) are importable from `parse_apis`. On a caught error read `str(e)` (the actionable message), `e.code` (the stable wire kind), `e.status_code` (the Parse GATEWAY's HTTP status), and `e.upstream_status_code` / `e.snippet` / `e.url` (the TARGET SITE's status, body excerpt, and URL when the gateway relayed one). APIs also declare typed per-API errors — subclasses listed in each README — you can catch by name. Retries: the SDK auto-retries ONLY gateway 429 on GET/HEAD (honoring `Retry-After`); everything else surfaces immediately.
- **Self-pacing (optional).** Each response's cost/limit headers are parsed onto `client.last_meta` (after a successful call) and `err.meta` (on a raised error): `credits_remaining`, `rate_limit_remaining` / `rate_limit_reset`, `retry_after`. Read them only if you want to throttle proactively — the SDK already handles 429 backpressure for you.
- **Source.** Generated from https://api.parse.bot. Re-run `parse sync` to refresh; do not hand-edit generated files.
